title: Add internal CLI: demo tenant bootstrap (org/projects/routes) with idempotency + env guards
author: Devon Price
description:
Context: Sales Engineering needs a repeatable way to stand up a production-like “demo tenant” (org + projects + routes + model pins) and reset it between demos without manual Console clicking. This PR adds an internal CLI command to bootstrap the demo tenant in an idempotent way and with explicit safety rails to prevent accidental execution against non-demo environments.

What’s included:
- New CLI command: `rw demo bootstrap` (internal-only) that creates/updates:
  - Demo org `redwood-demo`
  - Projects: `core-api`, `prod-econ`, `reliability`, `observability`
  - Routes for each project with pinned model versions (via route config), and baseline policy stubs for fallback (full policy enforced in ENG-4840)
  - Seeded API keys (scoped) for SE usage (key scoping tightened further in ENG-4855)
- Idempotent creation semantics: re-running the command is safe; resources are looked up by stable external IDs + naming convention, then patched to match the desired spec.
- Environment guards:
  - Requires `--env demo` OR `REDWOOD_DEMO_TENANT=1`.
  - Refuses to run if control-plane reports a non-demo org already exists with the same slug, or if billing account is not `billing-sandbox`.
  - Requires explicit `--confirm` for destructive updates (route overwrite, key rotation).
- Dry-run mode: `--dry-run` prints intended actions and exits non-zero if drift is detected (useful for pre-demo checks).
- Structured output: `--format json` emits a machine-readable summary used by the runbook/healthcheck followups.

Why this approach:
- Deterministic bootstrap makes demos resilient to Console/UI changes and avoids “dashboard emptiness” from missing routes/projects.
- Idempotency + drift reporting supports quick resets between demos and parallel demo namespaces (later work in ENG-4894).
- Guardrails reduce the blast radius risk (learned from prior internal RBAC/environment confusion in INT-993).

Testing:
- Unit tests for spec->API calls mapping, idempotent behavior, and env guard refusal logic.
- Manual: ran against `demo-control-plane` and re-ran bootstrap 5x to validate no duplicate org/projects/routes; verified output summary consumed by SE runbook.

Rollout notes:
- Behind internal feature flag `internal_tools.demo_bootstrap_cli`.
- Documentation stub added to internal docs (full runbook lives in Confluence; Elliot will link once published).

Follow-ups:
- ENG-4833: synthetic traffic generator to populate Console dashboards.
- ENG-4840: formalize model pinning + safe fallback policy and alerting on catalog drift.
- ENG-4855: key rotation + least privilege tightening.

review_conversation: Markus Klein (SE/demo owner): This is exactly what we need. Request: can we make project names stable and aligned to the talk track modules (core-api, prod-econ, reliability, observability)? Also please add a way to emit a summary for runbooks.
Devon Price (author): Updated spec to use stable external IDs and the module-aligned project slugs. Added `--format json` summary output including org_id/project_ids/route_ids + drift info.

Ethan Park (control plane/auth): Guardrails: I want a hard refusal if the billing account is not the sandbox one. Also require explicit confirmation for key creation/rotation—too easy to leak long-lived keys otherwise.
Devon Price (author): Added billing-sandbox validation call and gated key operations behind `--confirm`. Default is no key changes unless the user opts in.

Chloe Martin (Console backend): Can we avoid relying on display names for lookup? Slugs alone can drift; prefer external_id labels. Also watch out: route PATCH is partial and can drop fields if not careful.

Devon Price (author): Switched lookups to external_id where supported; otherwise fall back to (org_id, slug) with explicit checks. Route updates now use PATCH with a field mask to avoid clobbering unrelated settings.

Leila Farouk (QA automation): Please add tests that re-run bootstrap twice and assert no duplicates + no additional API calls on second run (or at least same IDs). Also add a refusal-path test (non-demo env).
Devon Price (author): Added idempotency tests with a fake control-plane client and a second-run assertion; added guard refusal tests for env != demo and missing confirmation.
Ethan Park: One more: require either `--env demo` or the env var, not both optional. I want this to fail loudly by default.
Devon Price (author): Done. The command now requires an explicit environment signal; default execution fails with a help message.
Markus Klein: Approved. Once merged I’ll update the SE checklist and request Confluence runbook updates.
Chloe Martin: Approved after field mask change. Thanks.
Leila Farouk: Approved. Tests look good.
release_notes: Internal-only: adds `rw demo bootstrap` to provision demo tenant resources idempotently with strong environment guardrails and machine-readable output for runbooks.
